incident.ghost_slot.detail: Slot held on {proxy} while device unavailable
incident.ghost_slot.idle_detail: Slot held on {proxy} with nothing exchanged with the device for {seconds}s (device not managed by Home Assistant)
incident.bond_lost.detail.one: {count} connection refused through {proxy}, which has no pairing key for this device. On its own this is harmless; if the count climbs, re-pair the device through {proxy}.
incident.bond_lost.detail.other: {count} connections refused through {proxy}, which has no pairing key for this device. Re-pair the device through {proxy} — each proxy keeps its own keys, so pairing through another one will not help.
incident.proxy_offline.detail: Proxy offline (no longer a registered scanner)
incident.proxy_stalled.detail: Online but no BLE advertisement seen for {seconds}s
notify.storm.title: BlueSight: pairing storm
notify.storm.message.one: {count} connection failure on {address} in {seconds}s. If this is a Daikin/BRC1H-type device, toggle its Bluetooth off and on, then trigger a reconnect.
notify.storm.message.other: {count} connection failures on {address} in {seconds}s. If this is a Daikin/BRC1H-type device, toggle its Bluetooth off and on, then trigger a reconnect.
notify.deadlock.title: BlueSight: proxy slot deadlock
notify.deadlock.message: {address} is holding a connection slot on {count} proxies at once ({sources}) with no working link — this stalls the connection pool (HA core issue #176516). Power-cycle the device or restart the affected proxies to release the slots.
notify.ghost_slot.title: BlueSight: ghost slot
notify.ghost_slot.message: A slot on {proxy} is held for {address} but the device is unavailable. If it stays stuck, restart that proxy to free the slot.
notify.ghost_slot_idle.title: BlueSight: idle slot
notify.ghost_slot_idle.message: A slot on {proxy} is held for {address} with nothing exchanged with the device for {seconds}s. This address is not a Home Assistant device, so nothing else can tell whether the link is alive. If the slot stays held, restart that proxy to free it.
notify.bond_lost.title: BlueSight: missing pairing key
notify.bond_lost.message.one: {count} connection refused for {address} through {proxy}: this proxy has no pairing key for the device. On its own this is harmless; if the count climbs, re-pair the device through {proxy} — each proxy keeps its own keys.
notify.bond_lost.message.other: {count} connections refused for {address} through {proxy}: this proxy has no pairing key for the device. Re-pair the device through {proxy} — each proxy keeps its own keys, so pairing through another one will not help.
notify.proxy_offline.title: BlueSight: proxy offline
notify.proxy_offline.message: Bluetooth proxy {address} is offline — check its power and Wi-Fi.
notify.proxy_stalled.title: BlueSight: proxy stalled
notify.proxy_stalled.message: Bluetooth proxy {address} is online but has received no BLE advertisement for {seconds}s — power-cycle it.
notify.proxy_reboot_storm.title: BlueSight: proxy rebooting
notify.proxy_reboot_storm.message.one: Bluetooth proxy {address} has rebooted {count} time in {seconds}s — check its power supply / for brownouts.
notify.proxy_reboot_storm.message.other: Bluetooth proxy {address} has rebooted {count} times in {seconds}s — check its power supply / for brownouts.
notify.unknown.title: BlueSight: incident
card.proxies.empty: No BlueSight proxies found. Once the integration is set up, sensor.<proxy>_slots_used entities appear automatically. You can also list them explicitly with the `proxies:` config option.
